claims.text: Post-processing additively manufactured BCC HEA components with deep cryogenic treatment improves dimensional precision.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the mechanical integrity of laser-additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr-family alloys.
Deep cryogenic treatment relieves residual stresses in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces phase transformations in additively manufactured BCC HfNbTaTiZr-family HEAs.
The phase transformations induced by deep cryogenic treatment reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Laser-additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr or similar BCC HEAs commonly contain residual stress, porosity, nonuniform grains, and distortion.
The proposed intervention is a long-duration deep cryogenic treatment after additive manufacturing.
Deep cryogenic treatment should be applied immediately after fabrication.
Deep cryogenic treatment produces HCP precipitates at grain boundaries.
Stress relief during deep cryogenic treatment enhances lattice distortion.
The treatment causes grain refinement and reduces residual-stress concentrations.
Cryogenic phase transformations promote nucleation of fine precipitates that refine the grain structure.
Residual-stress relaxation minimizes dimensional deformation in the treated components.
Deep cryogenic treatment enhances tensile strength and ductility relative to the as-deposited condition.
Deep cryogenic treatment enhances hardness.
Deep cryogenic treatment mitigates defects inherited from rapid solidification.
Treated specimens will exhibit less warping or distortion than as-deposited specimens.
Treated specimens will exhibit lower defect density and greater microstructural homogeneity than as-deposited specimens.
Deep cryogenic treatment will yield approximately 10–25% improvements in tensile strength and ductility relative to as-deposited material.
The effect should apply to laser-based additive manufacturing of BCC HEAs when residual stress and rapid-solidification defects are prominent.
